These 5 power words change the answer because they change the job ChatGPT thinks it's doing. 1. TRUTHMODE: Honesty instead of compliments. Put it before a prompt when you want the model to push back, name weak logic, and stop glazing. 2. /human: Text with less stiffness. One of the big "selling points" of AI is time saving, but the question I always have is: save time to do what? If you're using AI to skip out on the creation process of content creation, really all you're looking for is an end result, most likely being, you want something from others. You want people to engage, to give you money, to buy your product. I make videos because I LIKE making videos, and wouldn't you know, that's exactly why I've been able to grow an audience on social media. Social media is supposed to be SOCIAL. What's the point of putting fake junk on the internet? Why would anyone want a fake review of a book from a fake person? Content creators often complain about all of the bot traffic on social media now: comments, follows, and likes that aren't from real people, just dummy accounts...creating with generative AI tools is exactly the same thing just on the other side of the coin. To be honest, there are some actual useful applications for "AI" technology, but in my opinion, it shouldn't be anywhere near the actual creative elements of a process.  Learning new skills is a big part of the fun of this journey, and once you have those skills, they're yours forever. You don't have to worry about subscription prices going up, or models changing, and ultimately you end up with a deeper understanding of the creative process, which if you do choose to use an AI in the creative process, that deeper understanding will prove fruitful there anyway.
